text:
mira: heads-up, see a reproducible p99 spike under load when KV cache starts evicting rapidly. noticed it after the microbatch size tweak yesterday.
kevin: can you paste the perf trace and the config you used?
mira: here are the quick reproducer steps and the p99 timeline from perf-agent
```
# repro
ab-run --concurrency 120 --rate 6000 --payload tests/prompt_long.json --target http://localhost:8080/generate

# config snippet
microbatch: 32
max_batch_wait_ms: 8
kv_cache_size_mb: 1024
kv_eviction_policy: lru_adaptive

# perf tail (p95/p99) sample
00:00:00 load 50% p95 85ms p99 210ms
00:02:10 load 90% p95 110ms p99 620ms  <-- eviction onset
00:02:22 kernel_fallback_count +12
00:02:30 p99 980ms, queue depth jumped
```

kevin: kernel_fallback_count means we dropped into the slower matmul path? that's the expensive code path.
annA: (anna) that fallback + eviction churn is the classic fragility. microbatch=32 means larger KV working set per request.
mira: exact issue: under high concurrency, per-request KV insertion spikes, LRU churn causes many keys to be evicted between requests -> cache miss -> runtime chooses a fallback kernel for cold KV path and also can't leverage prefix caching -> latency multiplies.
tom: curious: did you try reducing microbatch to 8 or 4 to reduce working set overlap?
mira: yes, quick test:
- microbatch=8: p99 drops from 980ms -> 220ms, throughput down ~12%
- microbatch=4: p99 ~180ms, throughput down ~22%

sudha: so it's a SLO vs throughput tradeoff. We either accept lower throughput or pay p99 risk.
kevin: also look at KV eviction hysteresis. LRU adaptive is too eager. maybe add a small headroom and eviction delay or make cohort aware of microbatch size.
ops-bot: note created: ENGRT-1298 "investigate KV thrash -> kernel fallback" (assignee: kevin)
deploy-bot: rollout 2026-04-10T09:12:00 started for runtime v1.23.4 (canary)
anna: experiments to try:
- add `kv_reserve_ratio: 0.15` to keep cold prefix cache for active requests
- implement microbatch-aware admission (group requests that share prefix hashes)
- selective smaller microbatches when KV miss rates > 12%

kevin: i ran a sim overnight with kv_reserve_ratio 0.15 and microbatch 16 and saw p99 steady ~240ms at 95% load, throughput within 6% of baseline.
mira: profiler flame shows hot on `kv_lookup()` and `matmul_fallback()` during spikes. attaching snippet:
```
# stack sample (hot)
kv_lookup
kv_evict
matmul_fallback
dispatch_rpc
```

tom: can we do kernel selection earlier (heuristic based on expected kv-miss rate) so we avoid mid-inference fallback? that avoids the mid-run cost.
kevin: yes, plan: preflight pass checks estimated kv-hit-prob given microbatch size + prefix histogram => choose optimized kernel variant (kv-prefetched) vs fallback.
sudha: also alerting: add a metric `kv_eviction_rate` and an SLO-triggered autoscale policy to reduce concurrency on nodes when eviction_rate spikes.
mira: agreed. immediate action items:
1) kevin: prototype `kv_reserve_ratio` change + microbatch 16 test (today)
2) anna: add probe metric and dashboard for kv_eviction_rate and kernel_fallback_count (this afternoon)
3) tom: POC preflight kernel selection heuristic (WIP)
4) ops: add ENGRT-1298 links to runbook

kevin: one more note: quantization path increases kernel fragility; some quantized kernels can't handle evicted KV layouts gracefully -> fallback more often.
anna: add to runbook: if quantized model + high kv_eviction_rate -> auto-switch to single-instance low-latency mode.
mira: thanks all. i'll post raw logs & perf traces in the ticket. for now reverting microbatch to 16 on canary until we get kv_reserve_ratio tested.
kevin: 👍
anna: :thumbsup:
sudha: noted, i'll update oncall runbook.
mira: closing the loop here but will follow up in ENGRT-1298 with data."
